About this study

You'll compare pairs of computer-generated images and judge how much the texture changes between them. There are no right or wrong answers for most of the comparisons — we're measuring how the change looks to people.

It takes about 8 minutes. We record your responses, your response times, and basic information about your screen. We don't collect anything that identifies you personally.

You can stop at any time by closing the tab.

[Replace this paragraph with your institution's approved consent text and ethics approval number before launch.]

What to do

On each screen you'll see two rows. Each row holds two versions of the same image, differing in the size of the texture — the scale of the brush marks, grain, or pattern.

Your job is to decide which row changes more between its left and right image. Not which row has bigger texture overall — which row has the bigger difference.

  • Go with your first impression. Don't study them.
  • Judge texture size, not colour, brightness, or subject matter.
  • Some comparisons are close. Guess when you're unsure — that's expected.
